7 - Verify a 'Layanan Instalasi' (installation service) cart line correctly needs no editable quantity control
CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — originally shipped as a force_fail defect from a client-supplied screenshot showing a "Layanan Instalasi" (installation service, Rp 100.000,00) cart line with no quantity control, unlike a normal ZINCALUME® steel SPANDEK® OPTIMA 0.40 x 6000mm line beside it which showed a real qty input ("600"). The client's own follow-up clarified the intended business rule: an installation/site-visit service is inherently a fixed qty-of-1 item, so it does NOT need an editable quantity control at all — the original absence was correct behavior, not a defect. Corroborated live: opened the PDP's own "Survey Bangunan & Instalasi" modal (`.pdp-btn-survey`) and confirmed its step-2 "Inspeksi Lokasi Pembangunan" section shows the identical fee text ("Biaya pengecekan Rp100,000") matching the screenshot's price exactly, and step 1's contact fields ("Nama Kontak", "Nomor Kontak", "Tujuan Pembangunan") match the screenshot's detail lines exactly, confirming the flow that produces this cart line is the real, correct source, not a rendering glitch or an unrelated feature. This also corrects an assumption made during the Checkout module's own investigation, which described this same "Survey & Instalasi" flow as one that "skips Cart and goes straight to Payment" — that was wrong for this specific step 1 ("Pembelian Material + Pengajuan Instalasi") sub-flow, which clearly DOES add a real fee line to the ordinary Cart alongside physical products; only a different, separate site-visit request type may legitimately skip Cart, not confirmed either way here. NOTE: the full submission flow requires a real interactive map pin-drop (`+ Tambah Lokasi`) and server-matched vendor ("Tukang") selection that could not be reliably scripted end-to-end in the time available (the map/vendor step depends on live geolocation + a backend vendor-matching call that never populated under automation) — the modal/fee-text corroboration described above was done via a one-off live check, not encoded as this test's own steps, because a SEPARATE live check right afterward found the entire `.pdp-survey` wrapper is currently `display:none` for both guest and logged-in sessions (the "Survey & Instalasi" button is present in the DOM but has zero size), so re-opening the modal is not reliably repeatable right now — likely a temporary state on this actively-developed staging site, not something to depend on for this test's own steps. This test's own steps therefore only confirm the PDP itself loads correctly; the business-rule correction (service items don't need a qty control) rests on the client's own clarification, not on live-reproducing the modal every run. Re-add the modal-opening/field-verification steps once `.pdp-btn-survey`'s wrapper is confirmed visible again.
Passed ▼

9 - [Negative] Verify setting quantity to 0 is blocked by the field's own native HTML5 validation (min=1)
CORRECTED 2026-08-13 — originally shipped as a force_fail defect ("no validation message appears anywhere"), disputed by the client's own manual testing ("properly working"). Re-investigated live per [[qa_reconciliation_workflow]]: the client was right, this was a false positive. The qty input has a real `min="1"` HTML attribute inside a form with no `novalidate`. Setting it to 0 via real keyboard typing (not Playwright's `.fill()`, which bypasses normal browser interaction) and tabbing away leaves `el.matches(':invalid')` true, `checkValidity()` false, `validationMessage` = "Value must be greater than or equal to 1.", and — confirmed via a network listener — the qty field's own `$el.form.requestSubmit()` auto-submit NEVER fires a request at all. The original investigation's methodology only scanned `document.body.innerText` for a custom app-rendered message element, which cannot see native browser constraint-validation UI (rendered outside the DOM/accessibility tree) — a real user typing 0 and tabbing away DOES see the browser's own native validation bubble pointing at the field, which is exactly the "clear validation message" this test was originally looking for. The "stale total" observed originally is correct behavior: the invalid submission was blocked, so nothing should have changed.
Passed ▼

20 - [Negative] Verify applying an invalid coupon code is rejected and does not change the total
Self-contained regardless of whether an earlier test (e.g. 19) left a real coupon applied to the session's cart — this test first removes any already-applied coupon (the "Hapus" button only exists when one is applied) before attempting to apply the invalid code, otherwise #coupon_code would still be disabled and showing the earlier code with no "Gunakan" button to click. IMPORTANT, confirmed live 2026-08-13: applying a coupon (valid or invalid) is a real full-page POST+redirect (302, confirmed via network capture), but REMOVING one is an async AJAX-based update with NO page navigation at all (confirmed zero `framenavigated` events) — waiting on `footer attached` after a Hapus click is a no-op (the footer never leaves), causing this test to race ahead before removal actually completes. Fixed to wait for the concrete signal that removal finished: `#coupon_code` losing its `disabled` attribute. Also, removal closes the `<details class="coupon-form">` accordion again as part of its own re-render (confirmed live), so the `expand_accordion` step below is required, not defensive boilerplate.

exact English phrase 'You used coupon code "%1".'.

`app/i18n/id_ID.csv`:
`"You used coupon code \"%1\".","Anda menggunakan kode voucher \"%1\"."`
then flush the translation cache (`bin/magento cache:flush` /
`translation`).

23 - Verify removing an applied coupon keeps the order summary (price totals and checkout button) visible and reverts the total
BLOCKED 2026-09-15 — same root cause as test 19: the "Test" coupon code this test depends on to have something applied in the first place is no longer valid (live-reconfirmed: 'The coupon code "Test" is not valid.') — see test 19's full [C] TEST-SIDE / INFRASTRUCTURE diagnosis. This test's own removal-flow logic (documented below) was never itself broken; it just can't run without a coupon successfully applying first. Originally authored as a force_fail case ("removing a coupon deletes the entire order-summary sidebar from the DOM") based on clicking an unscoped "css=button:has-text('Hapus')" selector — confirmed via live re-investigation that this selector's .first() match on a populated cart is actually the CART ITEM'S OWN delete button (aria-label "Remove ZINCALUME® steel SPANDEK® OPTIMA 0.40 x 6000mm - Gray", which also renders visible text "Hapus"), not the coupon form's own "Hapus" button, because the item's delete button appears earlier in the DOM. Clicking it deletes the whole cart item, correctly leaving no order-summary sidebar at all (same as the real empty-cart state tested in test 1) — a false-positive defect caused by selector ambiguity, not a real product bug. Re-tested with the button correctly scoped to ".coupon-form" and confirmed live (4 repeated checks) that removal works exactly as expected: the discount row disappears, the field re-enables and empties, the button label reverts to "Gunakan", the total reverts to the pre-coupon value, and .sh-cart-summary-col / #checkout-link-button both remain visible throughout.
